get_a_card.description: Get a Card. Returns the full service response for the connected account.
get_a_card.name: get_a_card

parameters.description: The ID of the card to retrieve.
parameters.name: card_id

availableBalance.description: What the card can spend right now, in `currency`, as a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units.

blockingReason.description: The single highest-priority reason this card is blocked — a card can hold several blocking reasons at once, so clearing this one may leave it blocked; do not present it as the only reason or as a complete unblocking instruction. Who/what has it blocked: user (a teammate — see userId/firstName/lastName), support (Spendesk support, identity never disclosed), controlRule (a company-configured spending control rule — could require a receipt, description, supplier, cost center, or custom fields depending on the company's rules; which rule and requirement is unmet is not exposed here), scheduledDeactivation (a recurring deactivation schedule configured for this physical card — reactivates automatically per that schedule), automatic (an automated process, no further detail exposed), or internal (an internal reason with no disclosable detail — contact the Spendesk support team for more information). Only populated while status is Blocked; null or absent otherwise. Use GET /v1/cards/:cardId/blocking-history for every reason on the card, active and past.

cardOrder.description: Physical card order/shipping info: state, city/country (not the full address), trackingLink, dates, consideredAsLost, estimatedReceivedAt. Only populated for physical cards while pre-activated (status Pre-activated); null or absent otherwise — this does not mean the order info no longer exists after activation, see GET /v1/cards/:cardId/order for the status-independent lookup.

consideredAsLost.description: Computed at read time, not stored: true when receivedAt is null and the order was placed more than 30 days ago. receivedAt is not reliably recorded, so this is only a possible delivery-delay signal while the card is still Pre-activated; ignore it once the card is Active, Blocked or Ready. Not the card's own Lost status — never report the card as lost or the shipment as delayed from it; read the card's status for that.

expiryDate.description: Expiry date printed on the card, set by the card provider. For multi-use cards this is NOT the date the card stops working — use multiUseCardExpiryDate instead.

lastSuccessfulPaymentTime.description: Timestamp of the last settled card payment. Explicit null means confirmed: the card has never had one. The field being absent from the response instead means the lookup temporarily failed and the status is unknown — do not treat a missing field as null.

multiUseCardExpiryDate.description: Expiration date of a multi-use card (ISO 8601 datetime): the end date chosen by the requester when the card was requested. Choosing an end date is mandatory when requesting a multi-use card, so this is set on every card of type multi_use; it is absent on all other card types. For multi-use cards it is the single source of truth for expiration — the date the card actually stops being usable — and always takes precedence over expiryDate.

recurrence.description: Payment recurrence of the subscription, normally null for non-subscription cards. MONTHLY is also the fallback when the recurrence could not be resolved (no linked request, no interval on it, or a failed lookup), so it is not a confirmed cadence.

request.description: The originating request behind this virtual card: id, label, and the amount/currency the requester declared when creating it. amount and currency are in the requester's chosen (declared) currency, which may differ from the card's top-level currency and availableBalance — those are always in the company's currency. amount is a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Null when the card has no linked request or when the request lookup failed — the two are not distinguished, and a failed lookup also nulls supplier and costCenter.

amount.description: Amount.

spendingLimit.description: The card's monthly budget, in `currency`, as a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Null when no monthly budget is set.

status.description: Card status label: `Active`, `Blocked`, `New`, `Ready`, `Pre-activated`, `Hidden`, `Unknown`, `Aborted`, `Lost`, `Stolen`, `Damaged`, `Expired` or `Cancelled`. A status code with no label is returned as the raw code, so treat unknown values as possible.

subscriptionBudget.description: The subscription's remaining budget as shown on the card in the product: budgetAmount (the declared budget), spentAmount (current billing period spend only, capped at budgetAmount), availableAmount (what is left of this period's budget; 0 when at or over budget), and spentPercent (rounded whole number 0–100; 100 can also mean just under budget). When the declared currency differs from the company's and the period's spend in the company currency, FX fees included, exceeds the budget, spentAmount, availableAmount and spentPercent are all 0, which means over budget, not unused. Use the card's transactions for actual spend. Amounts are in the subscription's own declared currency (the currency field here), which may differ from the card's top-level currency and availableBalance — those are always in the company's currency. All amounts are decimals in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Only populated for subscription cards; null or absent otherwise.

Only present when `withApproval` is enabled. `steps` is ordered and holds only the approvers this request is actually waiting on, has been approved by, or was rejected by — it is empty when the request needed no approval (for example an auto-approved request).

byUserId.description: The user who approved or rejected, which is the delegate on a delegated step.

reason.description: Reason given with the decision. Approvers are not asked for one when approving, so this is usually only set on a rejection.

invoiceId.description: Id of the credit note document, served with invoices, which differs from the request id.

invoiceRequestData.description: Only present on `invoice` requests, which are returned only to tokens that also hold the `experimental:invoice:read` scope. Null when the invoice record is missing.

dueDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Null when not captured yet.

invoiceId.description: Id of the invoice document, which differs from the request id.

invoiceNumber.description: Number the supplier gave the invoice. Null when not captured yet.

distance.description: Distance of the journey, in `distanceUnit`, with 2 decimals at most.

multiUseCardEndDateChangeRequestData.description: Multi use card end date change request data.

multiUseCardTopUpRequestData.description: Multi use card top up request data.

days.description: Number of days the allowance covers.

purchaseOrderRequestData.description: Only present on `purchase_order` requests, which are returned only to tokens that also hold the `experimental:purchase-order:read` scope.

netAmount.description: Amount net of taxes, in the currency of the request, as a monetary value whose `amount` is expressed at `precision` decimals. Unlike `requestedAmount`, it does not use two implied decimals: read `precision` before comparing the two.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest currency unit (e.g., cents for USD)

precision.description: Number of decimal places (e.g., 2 for USD)

purchaseOrderId.description: The purchase order opened when the request was approved. Null while the request is not approved.

requestedAmount.description: Amount declared on the request, in `currency`, as an integer with two implied decimals whatever the currency: 1250 is 12.50 EUR and 100000 is 1000 JPY. Divide by 100 to get major units. Null when the request has no amount. On a `subscription_increase` request, this is the new budget asked for the subscription, not the increase. On a `purchase_order` request, this is the amount of the purchase order asked for; `purchaseOrderRequestData.netAmount` is its net of taxes counterpart, in a different encoding. On an `invoice` request, this is the gross amount of the invoice. On a `credit_note` request, it is negative, as the credit note reduces what the company owes the supplier: a credit note may already have been deducted from an invoice or refunded outside Spendesk, so do not net it against invoice amounts.

teamId.description: Team the request is attributed to.

data.description: A payable is a short-term liability owed by a company to its creditors (suppliers or employees). Several types of payables are supported by Spendesk, e.g. Invoices, Credit Notes, Expense Claims, Physical card purchases, Single Use card purchases, Subscription card purchases, etc.

This feature is not activated by default.
If activated, `accounting date` field allows accountants to override the original expense date.
In the `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

allocations.description: An array of allocations for the payable. An expense payable can have a settlement or a reversal payable allocated to it. A reversal payable can have a settlement or an expense payable allocated to it.

allocatedAmount.description:
If the payment was made in a foreign currency, this amount will be the one in the payment currency.
Can contain a negative value in case of refunds.
Expressed in smallest units of the currency (e.g. cents for EUR and USD, but yen for JPY).

from.description: Start date of the amortisation period. In the ISO 8601 date-time format.

to.description: End date of the amortisation period. In the ISO 8601 date-time format.

amount.description:
If the payment was made in a foreign currency, this amount will be the one in the payment currency.
Can contain a negative value in case of refunds.
Expressed in smallest units of the currency (e.g. cents for EUR and USD, but yen for JPY).
amount.title: priceAmount

items.title: analyticalProperties

appUrl.description: Link to this payable in the Spendesk web app.

bookkeepingStatus.description:
Status of the payable in the Spendesk flow. 

| Status | Description |
| ---|--- |
| `created` | Payable (approved expense) has been created. There is no accounting or supplier information on the payable in this state. |
| `prepared` | Payable has been prepared (enriched with accounting and supplier information) by an accountant. |
| `exported` | Payable has been exported to accounting |
| `failedExport` | Payable has failed to export to accounting via a native Spendesk integrations |
| `exportedManually` | Payable has been marked as exported manually by the accountant |
| `unprepared` | Payable has been sent back to Bookkeep>Prepare |
"

commitmentCounterparty.description: The spending commitment counterparty, when available. For expense claims, a supplier reference identifies the merchant while counterparty identifies the employee being reimbursed. The merchant name is available from the payable detail response; never use the employee accountPayable as a merchant creditor account.

counterparty.description: The supplier or employee counterparty for this expense.

creationDate.description: Issue date of the payable — the date on the underlying document: a supplier invoice's issue date, or for card purchases the transaction's settlement date. This is the payable's accounting-relevant business date and the default basis for placing it in an accounting period. It is set during the request/review flow, is editable by controllers, and can be backdated, so it does NOT reflect when the record entered Spendesk (see firstCreatedAt for that). When the optional accounting-date override is enabled, accountingDate takes precedence for the booking period; otherwise accountingDate defaults to this date. To filter payables by this date, use the payableDate date-filter field (this same value is returned here as creationDate) — not firstCreatedAt, which is the system-entry timestamp.
